report:
Your results match your rating: you scored 50% against an expected 49% [F1], and you blunder slightly less than similar-rated players would in your positions (0.97 times the expected count [F2]).

## Biggest weaknesses
No opening shows a clear weakness once rating, sample size and the number of openings checked are taken into account [F9]. The model also found no excess blunders overall [F2]. What follows is one thing to keep an eye on, not a confirmed problem.

1. **Scotch Game as Black (worth watching, small sample).** You scored 21% against 46% expected over 12 games [F8]. Across 34 openings, one result this extreme is expected by luck alone [F8]. In moves 13-25 you lost 6.2 win% per move here, against 5.1 across all your games [F15]. Your worst games include the Goring Gambit Declined (4.c3 d5 5.Bb5) and the Scotch Gambit (4.Bc4 d6) [T1]. One of those also had your 43...Kh7, which lost 93 win% when Qxf4+ was available [F16][T1]. *What to do:* choose one reliable answer to 4.c3 and one to 4.Bc4, and replay these three games [T1] to find where the middlegame went wrong.

## What's working
- **Clock management under pressure.** With under 10% of your clock left, you made 0.85 times the expected blunders [F3]. With 10-30% left, it was 0.83 times [F4]. Your mistakes happen with plenty of time left (1.02 times expected [F5]), which points to calculation errors rather than time trouble.
- **Queen's Gambit as White.** You scored 60% against 50% expected (possible strength) [F6], with a median eval of +1.0 after move 12 [F13]. The Four Knights as Black also looks promising: 72% against 49% expected [F7].

## Training plan
- Do short sessions of middlegame puzzles: https://lichess.org/training/middlegame [F19]. The middlegame is where you blunder most often, on 6.7% of moves [F11].
- Before each move when you have time, check which pieces are hanging. Practise with https://lichess.org/training/hangingPiece [F20]. For an example, see 7...h5, which missed Nxg4 [F17].
- Look at your biggest single swings, such as 38...Qh2+ where Bf6 was better [F18]. Ask yourself whether you slowed down enough before playing a check.
- Fix your Scotch repertoire as described above, then check again after more games [F8].
- Keep playing the Queen's Gambit, and in moves 13-25 aim to turn your opening advantage into a win [F13].
